When the `@pnpm/exe.<target>` package is missing, `bin/pnpm.mjs` downloads the native binary on first run. Unless `COREPACK_NPM_REGISTRY` was set, it always went to registry.npmjs.org, even on machines configured for a mirror. It now reads the npm config.

prs.title: fix(config-deps): apply minimumReleaseAge when resolving config dependencies
prs.author: spencerbeggs
prs.body:
## Summary

Since pnpm/pnpm#16613 (11.28.5 and 12.10.0), pnpm verifies locked config dependencies against the registry before installing them, and that verification enforces `minimumReleaseAge`. Resolving a config dependency never applied `minimumReleaseAge`, in either CLI. As a result, `pnpm install` or `pnpm add --config` could record a config dependency version that a later clean `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` rejects.

This PR keeps the age gate on verification, because a config dependency's pnpmfile runs on every install. It closes the gap from the other side: resolution now applies the same cutoff.

- **pnpm v12 (Rust):** `ConfigDependencyVerification` carries a `resolution_policy` holding the `minimumReleaseAge` cutoff and `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`, built from `PickPolicy`. Resolving a config dependency or one of its optional subdependencies passes that policy to the resolver and rejects a result that carries a policy violation.
- **pnpm v11 (TypeScript):** the new `createConfigDepResolver` in `@pnpm/installing.env-installer` passes `publishedBy`/`publishedByExclude` to `resolveFromNpm` and throws on a policy violation. Both `resolveAndInstallConfigDeps` and `resolveConfigDeps` (`pnpm add --config`) use it. An optional subdependency's age violation fails the install, the same way a trust downgrade does.

A violation fails with `ERR_PNPM_BAD_CONFIG_DEP` and the verifier's message. A `version+integrity` pin resolves without the cutoff, because it only needs its tarbal

prs.author: lazerg

## Summary

A removal override such as `"debug>supports-color": "-"` did nothing when the package declares the optional peer only in `peerDependenciesMeta`, with no `peerDependencies` entry. `debug@4.4.3` and `follow-redirects` do this. The resolver treats such an entry as an optional `*` peer, but the overrider only walked `peerDependencies`, so the meta entry stayed and a sibling workspace project could still supply the peer.

In v12, `apply_to_arc` skips manifests that no override applies to, so that check now counts these entries too.

With this change the issue's script gives `debug@4.4.3` with no peer suffix, the same as `ws`.

Fixes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16681

fix(hoist): remove each parent of stale workspace links once
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16690.

`pruneStaleWorkspaceHoists` removed the empty parents of all stale workspace links in parallel. Links under one scope share `node_modules/@scope`, so several `rmdir` calls ran on the same directory at once. On Windows, removing a directory whose delete is still pending fails with `EPERM`, and that failed the install.

The cleanup now runs once per parent directory. A workspace alias has at most a scope directory above it, so the parents never overlap and the cleanup stays parallel.

On the side question in the issue: an empty `next` is intended. The hoisted linker unlinks every prior workspace hoist before it writes the tree (`unlinkPriorWorkspaceHoists` in `linkHoistedLayout.ts`), because a package that takes over a project's name would otherwise be written through the symlink into the project. The links are created again after the tree is linked.

pnpm v12 is not affected. It prunes workspace hoists one at a time and ignores scope-directory removal errors.

## Test

Added a test that mocks `fs.promises.rmdir` to fail with `EPERM` while a removal of the same directory is still pending, as Windows does. Without the fix it fails with the error from the issue. With the fix it passes on any OS.

prs.author: altaywtf
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpm no longer panics with "unexpected error when polling the I/O driver" under QEMU user-mode emulation, such as a `linux/amd64` image on Apple Silicon.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16696

- **Cause:** QEMU intercepts `open("/proc/self/exe")` and returns a stale descriptor number. In pnpm that number was tokio's epoll fd. Libc detection read it (EINVAL), then closed it, so the I/O driver's next `epoll_wait` failed.
- **Fix:** `pnpm/crates/detect-libc/src/elf.rs` opens the path from `std::env::current_exe()` instead. QEMU emulates `readlink` correctly. If the open fails, the existing `ldd` and `getconf` fallbacks still run.
- **v11:** not affected. It runs on Node and has no code like this.
- **No automated test:** the bug only reproduces under QEMU user-mode emulation, which the test suite doesn't run. Proof is the manual run below.

QEMU syscall trace from the published image (`QEMU_STRACE=1`):

...

...
epoll_wait(3,...,1024,57203,0,0) = -1 errno=22 (Invalid argument)

fix(network): end a close-delimited metadata body at an unclean TLS close
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16704.

`pnpm view` (and resolution in `pnpm update`) failed behind a TLS-intercepting proxy with `ERR_PNPM_RESOLVING_NPM_RESOLVER_BODY_READ_ERROR ... peer closed connection without sending TLS close_notify`.

The proxy sends the packument with no `Content-Length` and no chunked framing and ends it by closing the TCP connection without a `close_notify` alert. hyper reads such a body until EOF, and rustls reports that EOF as an error. Node.js treats it as the end of the body, so pnpm v11 works behind the same proxy.

Reproduced locally with a Python TLS server that sends a close-delimited response (plain and gzipped) and closes without `close_notify`: `pnpm@11.28.5 view` printed the version, the v12 build failed with the reported error, and with this change it prints the version.

reqwest has no hook to wrap the connection stream, so the fix sits at the body read. The new `pnpm_network::read_self_delimiting_text` keeps the bytes received before an unclean TLS close when the response has neither `Content-Length` nor chunked `Transfer-Encoding`, and both metadata fetch paths use it. A framed body cut short by the close still fails as an incomplete body, as it does in Node.js. Decompression drops `Content-Length`, so a cut-short gzipped body is rejected by the JSON parse instead, and the resolver already retries decode failures.

v11 is not affected, so this changes only v12.

prs.title: fix: keep built and patched slots on a repeat install
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16705.

A repeat `pnpm install` that misses the repeat-install fast path (for example under `recursiveInstall: false`, or with a root `file:` dependency) re-imported every patched package and every package with a build script into its project-local virtual-store slot, and reran builds whose side-effects cache had nothing to restore. The snapshot plan correctly left those slots alone, but `BuildModules` still walked every build/patch candidate reachable from the importers. A side-effects cache hit then re-imported the overlay, because only the global virtual store checks whether a slot already carries it.

The isolated linker now scopes the build phase like the hoisted linker already does. It considers only the snapshots this install materialized, plus those the previous install's `.modules.yaml` recorded as unbuilt (`pendingBuilds`/`ignoredBuilds`), so a previous `--ignore-scripts` install still gets built. A rebuild or an `allowBuilds` change still considers every candidate. The global virtual store and the hoisted linker keep their existing handling.

pnpm v11 is not affected: it builds only new nodes on this path (`depsToBuild: newDepPaths`), so this is a v12-only fix.

fix(store-dir): vacuum index.db after store prune deletes rows
prs.author: dnalborczyk
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm store prune` deleted rows from `index.db` but never reclaimed the freed pages. The database uses `auto_vacuum = NONE`, so a long-lived store's index kept growing (the issue reports 82% free pages). pnpm v11 runs `VACUUM` in `StoreIndex.deleteMany`; `StoreIndex::delete_many` in the Rust store now does the same, followed by `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`.

The checkpoint matters in WAL mode: `VACUUM` writes the rebuilt database into the WAL, and the main file only shrinks when that is checkpointed. The checkpoint also truncates the WAL that the `VACUUM` filled.

v11 already vacuums, so this is a v12-only fix.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16717

## Squash Commit Body

```text
StoreIndex::delete_many committed the deletes and left the freed pages
in index.db, which uses auto_vacuum=NONE, so a pruned store's index never
shrank. pnpm v11 runs VACUUM in StoreIndex.deleteMany; this matches it and
adds a wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) so the main file actually shrinks and the
WAL holding the rebuilt database is truncated.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16717
```

feat(pnpr): let admins manage teams through the npm team API
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the pnpr runtime-administration plan in pnpm/tasks#111.

- Adds an admin role (`auth.admins`) and per-registry `teamsManagedBy: config | api`. The default, `config`, keeps today's behavior.
- On an `api` registry, admins can use `pnpm team create/destroy/add/rm`. The endpoints that currently answer `teams_config_managed` now do the work.
- Team membership becomes live: `team:` access tokens read a swappable per-registry `TeamDirectory` instead of a member set copied when the config is compiled.
- The roster is stored in the hosted store (`.team-rosters/v0/<registry>.json`) with compare-and-set writes. Every replica rereads it at most 10 seconds after it changes.
- The registry directory now reports `admin` and each hosted registry's `teamsManagedBy`. The web UI uses this to show edit controls.
- CORS allows `PUT`, `POST`, and `DELETE`, so the web UI can send the edits.

| Method | Path | Effect |

prs.body:
## Summary

Phase 4 of the pnpr runtime-administration plan in pnpm/tasks#111: map OIDC groups to registry teams.

```yaml
auth:
  oidc:
    - name: company
      login:
        users: [...]
        groups:
          claim: groups          # default
          teams:
            - group: platform-engineers
              registry: private
              team: platform
```

A browser session whose ID-token claim lists `platform-engineers` is a member of `platform` on `private` for as long as the session lasts (at most an hour).

### Design

- **Session-scoped, not written to the roster.** `Identity::User` gains `memberships: Arc<[Membership]>`, where a `Membership` is a registry's `TeamDirectory` plus a team name. A `team:` token admits a member of its roster, or a credential carrying a membership of that same roster's team; directory equality is pointer equality, so a membership cannot reach another registry's team of the same name.
  - Removing someone from a group in the identity provider takes effect at their next sign-in, within an hour. A roster write would instead keep them in the team until their next OIDC sign-in, possibly forever.

- **Split across crates.** The auth crate maps the claim to `OidcTeamGrant`s at sign-in and keeps them on the session (`SessionUser`). The server resolves grants to live team directories per request (`oidc_groups::session_identity`).

prs.title: feat(pnpr): make rule changes conditional on the version they read
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Optimistic concurrency for the package rules admin API. This is a follow-up of pnpm/tasks#111 and answers the review point on https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/16732 that a reset could erase another admin's change.

- `GET /-/pnpr/v0/admin/rules/{ecosystem}/{name}` reports the version of the registry's stored changes, as `version` in the body and as the `ETag`.
- `PUT` and `DELETE` take `If-Match`. If the stored changes have moved on, the request answers **412** with `precondition_failed` and changes nothing. Without `If-Match` the last change still wins, so existing clients keep working.
- A reset now stores the empty set of changes rather than removing the record. It goes through the same compare-and-set as every other write, so a conditional reset has no gap between its check and its write.
- The version is the SHA-256 of the stored record, or `config` before any change is stored. GET builds the rules view and the version from one read of the stored record, so a replica that has not reloaded yet still hands out a matching pair. PUT answers with the rules it stored.
- `If-Match` is compared strongly and may list several tags. `*` is unconditional, a weak tag never matches, and an unreadable header answers 400.
- CORS allows `If-Match` and exposes `ETag` for the web UI. The UI half is Bit change request https://bit.cloud/pnpm/pnpr/~change-requests/rules-if-match.

## Summary

`npm access grant`, `npm access revoke`, and `npm access list packages <scope:team>` on a registry with `rulesManagedBy: api`. Follow-up of pnpm/tasks#111.

- `PUT /-/team/{scope}/{team}/package` with `{package, permissions}` adds `team:<team>` to the package's `access` list. `read-write` adds it to `publish` too, and `read-only` removes it from `publish`. Returns 201.

- `GET /-/team/{scope}/{team}/package` lists the `packages:` keys whose `access` names the team and admits the caller, as `{"<key>": "read-only" | "read-write"}`.

- A grant goes through the same read-modify-write compare-and-set as the rules admin API (`update_rules`), starts from the lists that apply now, and stores only the lists it changes, so untouched lists keep following the YAML.
- Changes need an admin caller and a team the roster holds. Registries without `rulesManagedBy: api` answer 403 with `rules_config_managed`.

The request bodies match what npm's `libnpmaccess` sends.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Makes pnpm a Rust toolchain installer. With `cargo.enabled`, `pnpm install` reads rustup's toolchain file (`rust-toolchain.toml`, or the older `rust-toolchain`) and installs the toolchain it names. This follows the way pnpm already provisions a Python interpreter.

A Rust toolchain is not a runtime, so the toolchain file is the source of truth. There is no `rust@runtime:` specifier and no `devEngines.runtime` entry. The same file is read by rustup, IDEs, and CI.

- **Lookup:** the nearest toolchain file at or above each Cargo manifest, never above the checkout.
- **Channels:** exact versions (`1.95.0`), minor lines (`1.95`), `stable`, `beta`, `nightly`, and dated channels. `profile` (`minimal` or `default`, without `rust-docs`), `components`, and `targets` are honored. A file that sets `path`, has no channel, names a linked toolchain, or asks for another profile (such as `complete`) is left to rustup, as is a machine Rust publishes no toolchain for.
- **Trust:** the channel manifest is verified against the embedded Rust release signing key, and the release it describes must be the one the channel names, so a mirror cannot substitute an older signed release. A moving channel also refuses a release older than the one it last resolved to. Each component archive is checked against the SHA-256 the signed manifest names. `tools.rust.mirror` is honored, and is accepted only from global config, like the other tool mirrors.

feat(shim): run the Rust toolchain a project names from bare cargo and rustc
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#16741. That PR made `pnpm install` provision the Rust toolchain `rust-toolchain.toml` names, but only `pnpm run`, `pnpm exec`, and pnpm's own install-time calls used it. This PR makes the bare commands in a shell switch per project too, the way `pnpm shim add yarn` and the `node` shim do.

`pnpm shim add rust` adds project-aware shims for `cargo`, `cargo-clippy`, `cargo-fmt`, `clippy-driver`, `rustc`, `rustdoc`, and `rustfmt`, recorded under the `rust` key of `globalShims`.

- **Which toolchain:** the nearest `rust-toolchain.toml` (or `rust-toolchain`) at or above the working directory decides, read as rustup reads it.
- **Install on first use:** the toolchain is installed on first use through `pnpm_rust_toolchain::install_toolchain`, under the trusted configuration anchored in pnpm's state directory (`global-shim-rust`). A project cannot redirect the store the executable comes from.
- **How it runs:** the tool runs with the toolchain's `bin` first on `PATH`, so `cargo` finds the same toolchain's `rustc` without going back through the shim. It also gets `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` set to the toolchain directory, so a rustup proxy that Cargo finds first in `$CARGO_HOME/bin` (`cargo-clippy`, `cargo-fmt`) runs the same toolchain. An installed toolchain runs without building the async runtime or the HTTP client.
- **Trust:** a toolchain file selects only a release the Rust project signed, and the signature and the release are checked against the request.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpm v11's `rebuild` accepts `skipIfHasSideEffectsCache`, and teambit/bit called it with that option set to `true`: a package whose build the side-effects cache already holds is not built again. The `rebuild` function in `@pnpm/napi` had no such option, so every selected package ran its build scripts again.

This adds `skipIfHasSideEffectsCache` to the `rebuild` options of `@pnpm/napi`.

- `RebuildOptions` in `pnpm-deps-restorer` gets `skip_if_has_side_effects_cache`. An explicit rebuild normally bypasses the side-effects `is_built` gate. With the flag set, it keeps that gate, so a cache hit restores the cached build into the slot and the scripts do not run. The allow-build policy and the selection gate are unchanged.
- The napi binding reads `skipIfHasSideEffectsCache` from the options object. `index.d.ts` declares it on a new `RebuildOptions extends InstallOptions`, and the README row for `rebuild` mentions it.
- `rebuild` moves into `install/rebuild.rs` to keep `install.rs` under the file-length limit.

Behavior difference from v11: on a cache hit, v11 only skips the scripts. v12 also re-materializes the cached build output into the slot, the same way a warm install does.

pnpr serves its web UI at `/-/ui/` from its own origin, so the UI needs no CORS setting and no server URL. The UI ships as a separate npm package, `@pnpm/pnpr-ui`, that `@pnpm/pnpr` declares as an optional peer dependency:

```sh

```

The UI source stays on bit.cloud (`pnpm.pnpr/apps/pnpr-web`). This repository only pins a version of it and builds it.

`pnpr/ui` pins `@pnpm/pnpr.apps.pnpr-web@0.2.4`, the version that takes a `baseUrl` prop (https://bit.cloud/pnpm/pnpr/~change-requests/served-base-url). Loaded through pnpr in headless Chromium, the built UI connects to the serving pnpr and lists its registries, with no CSP errors.
